B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The official pricing page lists the Otter MCP server with Basic, which is priced Free. It does not state a separate MCP charge.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Basic: Free. Pro: $8.33/user/month billed annually or $16.99/user/month monthly. Business: $19.99/user/month billed annually or $30/user/month monthly. Enterprise: custom pricing.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The listed MCP feature appears under the free Basic plan. The official Help Center also describes MCP for Enterprise AI applications; it does not specify whether plan eligibility varies by client or workspace.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: OAuth authorization is required. The user can access meetings they captured and meetings shared with them. The Help Center documents connecting from supported MCP clients; some client setup paths have limitations, including connecting ChatGPT through its web version.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor, workspace admin, end user, and client: Otter controls account and workspace availability; admins may manage connector availability; users authorize access and clients manage tool enablement/permissions.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official documentation describes three read-oriented tools; no tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are published. A third-party catalogue describes the connector as read-only. 2. Otter documents user authorization and client-side tool permission prompts; it recommends “Always allow” as a client setting. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or approval flow is documented. 3. OAuth scopes are profile:read and conversations:read. The Help Center says users can access meetings they captured and meetings shared with them. Admin connector availability is mentioned; token lifetime and MCP-specific admin switches are not specified. 4. No read-only mode, toolsets filter, query-free mode, sandbox, or regional endpoint was found. Client interfaces let users enable the connector and manage tool permissions. 5. The documented meeting boundary is captured or shared meetings. get_user_info exposes name and email. No field masking or PII exclusion for MCP is documented. 6. No MCP rate limits, quotas, result caps, truncation, or per-call costs were found. 7. Official tool parameter schemas and validation/correction behavior are not published. 8. Otter pricing advertises Business activity logs and usage analytics, but does not say whether MCP calls are recorded. MCP telemetry details are not published. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or report tool is listed in the official tool list. No MCP result upsell was found. 10. No server-delivered behavioral instructions or skills were published. Client setup documentation recommends accepting tool requests and suggests enabling Always allow; these are client-level directions. 11. No persistent agent memory or behavior-dependent tool availability is documented. 12. The input is a hosted Otter meeting-data endpoint. Otter also describes its AI Chat acting as an MCP client to external services; that is a separate product direction, not a documented sub-server here. 13. No raw API, arbitrary query, SQL, or script execution tool appears in the official list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: We recommend setting it to Always allow.
If prompted, accept the tool request to proceed.
If you are experiencing any issues querying your Otter conversations, we recommend specifically mentioning the Otter tool you want to use in your query.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The input endpoint is documented as one hosted endpoint with a flat list of three tools. Otter's separate AI Chat MCP-client feature does not establish a hierarchy within this server.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public server code or complete official tool definitions including input schemas and initialize instructions were available to serialize.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The official MCP list exposes only profile lookup, meeting search, and transcript fetch; it publishes no Otter write operations. Otter's product and public API documentation describe additional capabilities such as recording and broader access to channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details. The public API is Enterprise-only and uses API keys; these API operations were not listed as MCP tools.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The Help Center advises users to accept client tool requests, set permissions to “Always allow,” and name the Otter tool in queries when troubleshooting. These are client-use recommendations; server enforcement is not documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Otter states: “All access is OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions.” It also says: “Your AI assistant can only access meetings you explicitly authorize.” The Help Center says accessible meetings include those captured by the user and those shared with them. The privacy policy describes training its proprietary AI on de-identified audio recordings and transcriptions, which may contain Personal Information; it does not specify MCP-specific data handling or whether MCP-accessed content is used this way.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Otter describes MCP as enabling transcript search across all time periods, analysis across meetings, and generation of content using meeting data. Its Help Center says users can click a source to open the Otter conversation.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth protection and the published read scopes are observable in endpoint metadata. The user-authorized-meeting boundary is documented, but no server-side per-meeting enforcement details are public. Client permission prompts and the Always allow recommendation are client-side. No public evidence links activity logs or privacy-policy training statements specifically to MCP calls.

contradictions: GrowthEngineer.ai lists search_transcripts, list_meetings, get_meeting_summary, and get_transcript, while the official Help Center and Claude connector list get_user_info, search, and fetch. The four catalogue names are retained as third-party-only entries; their status as separate endpoint tools is unverified.

Agent Discoverability reports three names with an otter_ prefix (otter_search, otter_fetch, otter_get_user_info), unlike the official names. These appear to correspond to the three official functions, but the listing is third-party and does not establish native tool names.

The official pricing page lists the Otter MCP server with the free Basic plan, while Otter's Help Center AI Chat FAQ describes connecting to other AI applications through MCP as an Enterprise-plan capability. The plan eligibility distinction is unclear.
observations_for_research: The OAuth metadata advertises profile:read and conversations:read scopes; the Help Center separately describes user authorization and access to captured or shared meetings.
The official Help Center publishes tool names and short descriptions but no parameter schemas, annotations, initialize instructions, or raw result definitions.
Otter presents both an MCP server for external AI clients and an AI Chat feature that can act as an MCP client to external services.
